groups.primary: the 30 states not scored in the linker comparison (the decider's cross-encoder trained on their twins, so its matches there are in-sample; the rule itself has no parameters)
groups.seen: the 7 states of the linker comparison, already inspected post hoc; secondary only

metrics.extra_links: links beyond the first per GRID3 facility
metrics.precision: links joining a facility to its twin / links whose GRID3 facility has a twin (every link counted; no best-per-facility pick)
metrics.twins_lost: twins the many-to-many decider crosswalk matched but the rule flagged

pass: on the primary group: one_to_one precision >= engine precision; one_to_one recall >= decider (many-to-many) recall - 0.1 points; twins_lost <= 0.1% of twins
question: Does a one-to-one rule (engine matches first, then decider matches by probability; later conflicting matches become duplicate flags) remove the decider's extra links without losing twins or precision?

rule.accept: greedily, at most one link per GRID3 facility and one per HFR record per state
rule.flags: a match whose GRID3 facility is already linked -> possible_hfr_duplicate; whose HFR record is already linked -> possible_grid3_duplicate
rule.ranking: engine matches first by engine score (descending), then decider matches by decider probability (descending), ties by decision id
rule.scope: the national crosswalk already produced (engine + nigeria-facility-decider-v1, decider spec sha256:3b37abf9...); no model or threshold changes

secondary: the same verdicts on the seen group
flags that sit on a twin (a twin kept out by an earlier non-twin link)
truth: GRID3 globalid = HFR global_id, same state; agreement with the registries' crosswalk, not accuracy
why: Post hoc in the linker comparison (7 states): the decider added 88 extra links (40 to 128), 75 of them a second HFR record for a facility whose twin was also matched, mostly HFR duplicates
